title: Evaluation of the profinite-point inverse image on a contractible affine
statement: Use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention] and the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $p_X^*=\pi_X^{-1}a^*$ be the geometric inverse image from sheaves on profinite sets defined in [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback]. Let $F$ be a sheaf of sets, abelian groups, or commutative rings on profinite sets with finite jointly surjective coverings. Let $U$ be an affine object of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ which is weakly contractible, meaning evaluation at $U$ sends epimorphisms of sheaves of sets to surjections. The quotient space $\pi_0(|U|)$ of connected components is profinite, and there is a canonical identification $(p_X^*F)(U)\cong F(\pi_0(|U|))$, natural in $F$ and in morphisms between such $U$. The identification preserves addition and multiplication when present. The topology on $\pi_0(|U|)$ is the quotient topology: a subset is open if and only if its inverse image in $|U|$ is open.

proof.text: For an affine weakly contractible $U$, the quotient $\pi_0(|U|)$ is profinite and maps from $U$ to the finite-quotient objects $X[S]$ are exactly continuous maps $\pi_0(|U|)\to S$, compatibly in $S$ and in $U$, by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-point-components-maps].

source.place: Lemma 4.2.13(1); exact master RefactorInstruction.tex, Section 4, proof of Lemma point-pullback formula.

proof.text: The left Kan extension defining the geometric inverse image $p_X^*=\pi_X^{-1}a^*$ evaluates on $U$ by the preceding finite-quotient correspondence: the resulting colimit is the value $F(\pi_0(|U|))$. This identification is natural in $F$ and in maps of weakly contractible affines, since all transition maps are induced by precomposition and the quotient map on components.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.13(1), inverse-image site computation; Hemo–Richarz–Scholbach Example 3.1.

proof.text: Because $U$ is weakly contractible, sheafification does not change this left-Kan-extension section on $U$: apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-sheafification-wcontractible-sections]. Thus the sheaf inverse image itself satisfies $(p_X^*F)(U)\cong F(\pi_0(|U|))$, with the same naturality.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.13(1), sheafification on weakly contractible objects.

proof.text: For abelian groups and commutative rings, the comparison is induced by the same maps of underlying sections; addition and multiplication are computed pointwise, so the bijection preserves those operations. The quotient topology assertion is exactly the definition of the topology on $\pi_0(|U|)$.
